title: Concluding Remarks: Phenomenological Design Thinking (Ch. 7)
offset_note: book = pdf - 2; locus format (p.N / pdf N)
sections: 1. Framing: the academia/practice gap refused; no off-the-shelf methodology; re-examine existing methods through phenomenology; phenomenological design thinking = an evolution of post-phenomenology (Folkmann epigraph)
2. Praxis: theory-informed cyclical practice; dissolving academia/industry + theory/practice walls; Dasein's care carries over to designed objects
3. Limits of deliverables: the persona critique (decontextualization, detached understanding); point out limits rather than replace methods
4. Primacy of things: experience design always has an object; present-at-hand/ready-to-hand as continuum; Ihde's four relations not ranked
5. Multistability: design with variability; usability testing becomes observing coping strategies
6. Problem-solution paradox: the hermeneutic circle of design; play; critique of waterfall/positivism; flexible forward-backward plans
7. Care: design as un-throwing (Oosterling); specialization as the condition of concern

8. Practice: phenomenology explains/augments rather than replaces; abductive push into the future; familiarization/de-familiarization + concealment/unconcealment; ethnography + diagramming (Ihde telescope)

9. Five summary statements (hedged design principles): humans exist in context; thinking does not always precede action; intention is not primary; objects are more than material; utility does not trump meaning
10. In Conclusion: the book's identity crisis; establish a base of knowledge others can build on; push into future possibilities
12. Synthesis arc: diagnostic-not-prescriptive signature; design as disposition/praxis

key_terms.gloss: Applying phenomenology to design as a medium of meaning formation; an evolution of post-phenomenology whose next step is grounded in design thinking; addresses both present and future of experience.
Theory-informed practice; a cyclical theory<->practice relation in which the process matters as much as the result; phenomenology's anti-dualist way of being-in-the-world.
Self-and-world conglomeration exhibiting care and concern over itself; this care carries over to how humans use designed objects, so designers must work around it.
Things are our means to knowledge; experience design = understanding systems of things and how humans experience them; experience design always has an object.
Heideggerian object-relations read not as exclusive categories but as a continuum of interaction in constant back-and-forth motion; invisibility/intuition therefore not a valid design goal in itself.
Embodied, hermeneutic, alterity, background human-technology relations; none qualitatively superior; designers determine the use contexts where each applies.
Technology use is not determined by designers but has multiple stabilities (use contexts); creative misuse beats the clearest affordances; design with it, not against it.

key_terms.term: problem-solution paradox / hermeneutic circle of design
key_terms.gloss: Parts connected to whole and whole to parts; requires fluid play between problem definition and solution exploration; causes ambiguity in plans/billing.
Oosterling's term: humans design to take an active part in the world; designers are named for the care they exhibit; care erodes when spread thinly, so maintain specialization.
Design's distinctive use of knowledge of the past to extend into future experiences; analytical and creative thinking with equal importance.
Key design movement: bring the familiar close then make it strange; enacted in ethnographic research disturbing hyper-familiar bias.
Macro/micro movement across a problem-solution space (diagramming, zooming); the designer's role includes deciding when to conceal and unconceal.
Users adopt devices as interpretive objects; objects affect users as much as users affect objects, sometimes changing the user; grounds the moral weight of design.
The goal of identifying and optimizing opportunities for creating meaning through interaction; shifts evaluation from measurable functionality to contextual meaning.

claims.text: Wendt deliberately offers no strict, off-the-shelf methodology; instead he re-examines existing design methods through the lens of phenomenology.
Phenomenological design thinking is an evolution of post-phenomenology; the next step in post-phenomenology is grounded in design thinking.
The academia/industry and theory/practice dichotomies are detrimental; knowledge-production and commercial success are wrapped up in one another, not mutually exclusive.
Dasein's care carries over to the use of designed objects, so designers must always work around that care.
A persona does not experience anything (humans do); personas are decontextualized, detached, theoretical formulations that reinforce Cartesian dualism even when rigorously researched.
The aim is not to replace old practices but to point out their limitations; the ways designers frame their practices make all the difference.
Experience design always has an object: it designs experience and therefore must also design the things that are experienced.

Present-at-hand and ready-to-hand are not exclusive categories but a continuum; so invisibility/intuition/readiness-to-hand cannot stand as design goals in themselves, being judged good or bad only by context of use.
Multistability makes meticulous certainty-seeking a pantomime; usability testing should become the observation of users' coping strategies, which are the core insights for future design.
The problem-solution paradox is the hermeneutic circle of design and calls for play; waterfall's hyper-linear positivism (gather-plan-execute) mirrors the Cartesian split and leaves no room to adapt.
Care erodes as it spreads thinly across concerns; complex projects need maintained specialization so designers can sustain concern for a manageable set of practices.
Nothing in the book is revolutionary: phenomenology explains, augments, and adds rigor to current practices rather than supplying new ones, because design is inherently phenomenological.

Design's most useful peculiarity is pushing into the future via the abductive gesture; the process plays back and forth between past and future through familiarization/de-familiarization and concealment/unconcealment.
New end-goals emerge only after interaction begins; thinking does not always precede action, and praxis generates theoretical models through practical outputs (the swim-lesson example).
Designer intention is not primary and is effectively irrelevant once a product launches; launch is a step toward understanding, not the end of design.

Objects are more than material: via Verbeek's mediation and Latour's hotel key, objects co-shape users and have systemic effects; designers advocate not only for users but for preferable worlds, and must resist dark patterns.
Utility does not trump meaning: products need not be functionally perfect to be used, and the interaction that creates meaning is the ultimate concern (Krippendorff's product semantics).
The book's stated goal is to establish a base of knowledge on phenomenological philosophy on which others can build, not a grand narrative redefining experience design.

interlocutors.name: Mads Folkmann
interlocutors.draws: Sets the challenge: design as a medium of meaning formation relating to and possibly changing the constituents of experience; addressing both present and future of experience.

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.work: Being and Time (present-at-hand / ready-to-hand; care; Dasein)
interlocutors.draws: Object-relations read as a continuum; behavior as goal-oriented; care/being-in as the model for how Dasein uses designed objects.

interlocutors.name: Don Ihde
interlocutors.draws: Four human-technology relations none of which is qualitatively superior; the telescope as figure for concealment/unconcealment in diagramming.

interlocutors.name: Peter-Paul Verbeek
interlocutors.draws: Users adopt devices as interpretive objects; objects affect users as much as the reverse, grounding the moral implications of design.

interlocutors.name: Bruno Latour
interlocutors.draws: The weighted keychain makes the return decision for guests, disclosing the activity/agency of objects.

interlocutors.name: Klaus Krippendorff
interlocutors.draws: The goal of design is to identify and optimize opportunities for creating meaning through interaction; shifts evaluation from functionality to meaning.

interlocutors.name: Henk Oosterling
interlocutors.draws: Humans design to take an active part in the world and shape experience rather than remain content with the present situation.

interlocutors.name: Carl Mitcham
interlocutors.work: (design as a mode of being-in-the-world; framed in intro, echoed here)
interlocutors.draws: Design as a modern mode of being-in-the-world informs the praxis framing.

design_principles.name: Diagnose limits, do not replace methods
design_principles.gloss: Recognize what existing methods (e.g., personas) lack and avoid using them beyond their capabilities; the framing of a practice makes the difference.

design_principles.name: Do not treat invisibility/intuition as a goal
design_principles.gloss: Ready-to-hand vs present-at-hand (and Ihde's relations) are context-judged modes, not a ranked target; choose interaction styles per use context and narrative point.

design_principles.name: Test for coping, not perfection
design_principles.gloss: Reframe usability testing as observing how users cope with problems (the core design insight) rather than removing un-intuitive features.

design_principles.name: Plan for forward-backward play (anti-waterfall)
design_principles.gloss: Build plans flexible enough to move between problem definition and solution exploration; treat design as situated, embodied, abductive, not positivist gather-plan-execute.

design_principles.name: Maintain specialization to preserve care
design_principles.gloss: On complex projects keep a degree of division of labor so designers focus and sustain concern, rather than spreading care thinly.

design_principles.name: Humans exist in context
design_principles.gloss: Treat documents (personas, use cases, diagrams) as thinking aids, not deliverables; the real value is understanding from thinking through the object, not the artifact.

design_principles.name: Thinking does not always precede action
design_principles.gloss: Design for emergent goals discovered in use (including negative goals); favor embodied praxis over the assumption that representation drives behavior.

design_principles.name: Intention is not primary; design with multistability
design_principles.gloss: Subordinate designer intent to adaptability; treat launch as a step toward understanding and multistable use as a source of serendipity, not a defect.

design_principles.name: Objects are more than material; advocate for preferable worlds
design_principles.gloss: Account for the mediating, world-changing, systemic effects of designed objects; take moral responsibility and refuse dark patterns.

design_principles.name: Utility does not trump meaning; design with meaning
design_principles.gloss: Optimize opportunities for meaning through interaction rather than chasing functional perfection; high value/meaning sustains use despite imperfection.

open_problems: No operational methodology: by explicit choice, only re-framings of existing methods, not a repeatable procedure (p.153 / pdf 155).
Measuring/communicating meaning is conceded to be delicate, contextual, and 'slippery to sell'; no method offered (p.164 / pdf 166).
Planning/billing under the problem-solution paradox: calls for flexible forward-backward plans but supplies no concrete model to replace waterfall (p.157 / pdf 159).
Defining the discipline and locating care: 'experience designer' stays ambiguous; specialization prescribed without a disciplinary boundary (p.157-158 / pdf 159-160).
Operationalizing multistability and capturing emergent end-goals are endorsed but ungrounded in method (p.162 / pdf 164).
Ethics of mediation in practice: 'advocating for preferable worlds' and resisting dark patterns asserted as responsibility without a decision procedure (p.163 / pdf 165).

ro_hooks.note: Design-lens analogue of the actualization-of-desire chain's refusal to split deliberation from the embodied movement that completes action (energeia realized in the doing).
Maps onto the chain's hinge where equipmental absorption is punctuated by breakdown/disruption that throws the agent back into deliberative comportment and renewed orexis-formation.
